# MapKit

<!-- generated:header (isim/tools/coverage-summary.py; do not edit by hand) -->
**Symbols:** 74.6% of Apple's iOS API (1092 of 1463, exact) · **Rows:** 18: 15 ✅ 1 🟡 2 ❌ · **iOS:** 3.0+
<!-- /generated:header -->

**Area:** [Location, personal data & sensors](../COVERAGE.md#location) · **Apple:** [MapKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/mapkit) · **Issues:** [`area:location`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Alocation)

## How isim implements it

- **Adapted:** an offline basemap drawn from Natural Earth polygons (`Land.swift`, `Basemap.swift`), search from the gazetteer, and directions from an OSRM server you run.

## API

| API / feature | Status | iOS | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| MapKit `MKMapView` (region, camera, map types, gestures, conversion) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted offline basemap: water and land (coastlines from Natural Earth's public-domain land polygons, 1:50m / 1:10m, in the SDK), a lat/lon graticule and a built-in list of world cities/landmarks (a label that would collide with an annotation view or its title is left out, as Apple Maps does; the map's dump text lists the labels drawn, tested by `test_personal_objc`); no roads or buildings (isim has no map data service) unless raster tiles come from a local cache (`ISIM_MAP_TILES` or `$ISIM_DATA/Library/Maps/Tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`, never downloaded). Heading (the map turned, compass shown while turned; a tap turns back to north) and pitch (perspective tilt up to 60°; adapted: iOS's limit varies with zoom), pan, pinch, two-finger rotate and tilt, double-tap zoom; animated region/camera changes (0.35 s, visible-region updates per frame); zoom range/boundary honoured; `showsCompass`, `showsScale`, `showsUserTrackingButton`. Tested (HelloMaps: `test_mapkit`, `test_map_camera`) |
| MapKit annotations (`MKAnnotation`, `MKPointAnnotation`, `MKMarkerAnnotationView`, `MKAnnotationView`, user location, selection, callouts) | 🟡 | ≤17 | iOS-style balloon markers (tint, glyph text/image, title, bigger when selected), image views, reuse/registration, callouts with accessory controls, `didSelect`/`didDeselect`, blue user-location dot from the simulated Core Location. `MKAnnotation`/delegates are Swift protocols (title defaults to nil). Clustering and dragging: the row below. Tested |
| Clustering and dragging: `MKClusterAnnotation` (`init(memberAnnotations:)`, `memberAnnotations`, `title`, `subtitle`), `MKAnnotationView.clusteringIdentifier`, `cluster`, `isDraggable`, `dragState`, `setDragState(_:animated:)`, `MKAnnotationView.DragState`, `MKMapViewDelegate` `mapView(_:clusterAnnotationForMemberAnnotations:)` and `mapView(_:annotationView:didChange:fromOldState:)`, `MKMapViewDefaultClusterAnnotationViewReuseIdentifier` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted (issue #417): annotation views that share a clustering identifier and overlap the frame of the group's first view (the highest `displayPriority`) show as one cluster annotation, regrouped as the map moves or zooms; the selected and the dragged annotation stay apart. The cluster comes from the delegate (else a plain `MKClusterAnnotation`) and stands at the middle of its members; a nil title becomes the first member's title and a nil subtitle "+N more"; its view comes from `viewFor`, the registered default cluster view or a marker with the member count as its glyph; members' `cluster` is that view. Cluster annotations are not in `annotations`. A long press on a draggable view (`longdrag` in scripts) lifts it 12 points and it follows the finger; the drop sets the coordinate of an `MKPointAnnotation` or an Objective-C annotation's `setCoordinate:` (a Swift class of the app's own is not moved: isim's coordinate type is not `@objc`), then the default `setDragState` goes starting → dragging and ending (or canceling) → none, each change told to the delegate. Collision hiding by `displayPriority` and `collisionMode` outside clusters is not done. Tested (HelloMaps -cluster: test_map_clustering_dragging; HelloPersonalObjC) |
| MapKit overlays (`MKPolyline`, `MKPolygon`, `MKCircle`, renderers, `MKTileOverlay`) | ✅ | ≤17 | renderers draw through `draw(_:zoomScale:in:)` in renderer coordinates as on iOS (adapted: one call for the visible part, not per tile), so subclasses can draw themselves; path renderers: `createPath`, fill/stroke properties and paths overridable, line join/cap/miter, `lineDashPattern`/`lineDashPhase`, `interiorPolygons` cut out, `strokeStart`/`strokeEnd`; `MKGradientPolylineRenderer` colours along the line; geodesic polylines; tile overlays (file URLs; others through URLSession). Tested (`test_mapkit`, `test_map_overlay_renderers`) |
| MapKit search, directions, Look Around, snapshots | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted, offline: `MKLocalSearch`/`MKLocalSearchCompleter` answer from Core Location's gazetteer + the basemap's cities (else `placemarkNotFound`); `MKDirections` routes and ETAs come from an OSRM server you run (`ISIM_ROUTING_URL`; without it `directionsNotFound`, isim never picks a server); Look Around scenes come from equirectangular panoramas you supply (`ISIM_LOOKAROUND` or `$ISIM_DATA/Library/Maps/LookAround/LAT,LON.jpg`; a cylindrical view turned by dragging, `MKLookAroundSnapshotter`), none elsewhere; `MKMapSnapshotter` renders the offline basemap for a region or a camera (heading; pitch not drawn). Tested (`test_mapkit`, `test_map_services`) |
| SwiftUI `Map` (`Marker`, `Annotation`, `MapPolyline`, `MapPolygon`, `MapCircle`, `UserAnnotation`, `MapCameraPosition`, selection, `mapStyle`, `onMapCameraChange`) | ✅ | ≤17 | on MKMapView; Annotation content is SwiftUI in a hosted view; `mapControls` draws `MapCompass`, `MapScaleView`, `MapUserLocationButton`, `MapPitchToggle` on the map (adapted: standalone controls outside a map draw nothing); legacy `Map(coordinateRegion:showsUserLocation:userTrackingMode:annotationItems:)` with `MapMarker`, `MapPin`, `MapAnnotation`. Tested (`test_swiftui_map`, `test_swiftui_map_legacy`) |
| Objective-C interface (`MapKit.framework`): `MKMapView` (region, center, annotations, overlays, user location, tracking), `MKMapViewDelegate` (with dragging and clusters), `MKAnnotation` (the app's own classes too), `MKPointAnnotation`, `MKClusterAnnotation`, `MKAnnotationViewDragState`, `MKUserLocation`, `MKPlacemark`, `MKAnnotationView` / `MKMarkerAnnotationView` / `MKPinAnnotationView`, `MKPolyline` / `MKPolygon` / `MKCircle` and their renderers, `MKMapItem`, `MKLocalSearch` (request, response), `MKCoordinateRegion` / `MKCoordinateSpan` and their functions | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: headers over the Swift overlay's classes (Apple's Objective-C names); an Objective-C `<MKAnnotation>` object is wrapped for the overlay's Swift protocol and given back as itself; the struct members are Objective-C categories. Not from Objective-C yet: the camera and map configurations, directions, the search completer, snapshots. Tested (HelloPersonalObjC, tests/ui/test_personal_objc.py) |
| Map features: `MKMapView.selectableMapFeatures`, `MKMapFeatureOptions`, `MKMapFeatureAnnotation` (`featureType`, `pointOfInterestCategory`, `iconStyle`, `title`), `MKMapFeatureAnnotation.FeatureType`, `MKIconStyle`, `MKMapItemRequest` (`init(mapFeatureAnnotation:)`, `getMapItem`, `featureAnnotation`, `mapFeatureAnnotation`, `cancel()`, `isCancelled`, `isLoading`) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: isim's basemap has no points-of-interest service, so its own labels are the features: landmarks are points of interest (category landmark, a star icon), cities territories; no physical features. A tap on a label of a selectable kind adds and selects an `MKMapFeatureAnnotation` (the delegate's `viewFor`/`didSelect` see it); deselecting removes it. `MKMapItemRequest` finds the place in the offline gazetteer, else an item at the feature. `selectableMapFeatures` was an `Int` before 0.28 (ABI note in `isim/abi/allowlist.txt`). Tested (HelloMaps -features: test_map_features; HelloPersonalObjC) |
| `MKUserTrackingBarButtonItem` (`init(mapView:)`, `mapView`) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: a bar button that cycles the map's tracking mode (none, follow, follow with heading) and shows the mode's location symbol. Tested (HelloMaps -features: test_map_features) |
| SwiftUI map features: `MapFeature` (`kind`, `title`, `coordinate`, `pointOfInterestCategory`, `backgroundColor`, `image`), `Map(…selection: Binding<MapFeature?>)`, `MapSelection` (iOS 18: `Map(…selection: Binding<MapSelection<V>?>)`, `value`, `feature`), `mapFeatureSelectionDisabled`, `mapFeatureSelectionContent`, `MKMapItemRequest(feature:)` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted, on MKMapView's feature selection (above): a tap on a landmark or city label selects it; the selection content (a `Marker` or an `Annotation`) stands at the feature. Tested (HelloMaps -swiftui-features: test_swiftui_map_features, every iOS version) |
| `MapReader`, `MapProxy` (`convert(_:from:)`, `convert(_:to:)`, `camera(framing:)`) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: the proxy converts through the MKMapView of the Map inside the reader (local or global coordinate spaces); `camera(framing:)` fits a region in the map's size. Tested (HelloMaps -swiftui-features) |
| `LookAroundPreview` (`init(initialScene:…)`, `init(scene:…)`), `MKLookAroundBadgePosition` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: shows the scene in the Look Around viewer (scenes come from panoramas you supply, as for `MKLookAroundViewController`); without one, "Look Around isn't available". Road labels, points of interest and the badge are not drawn. Tested (HelloMaps -swiftui-features) |
| Types not yet in isim (iOS 17 and earlier) | ❌ | ≤17 | not implemented, found by the 2026-10 sweep: `AnyMapContent`, `DefaultUserAnnotationContent`, `DynamicMapContent`, `EmptyMapContent`, `MapContentView`, `MapSelectable`, `MapSelectableContentView`, `TupleMapContent` (8 types; with their members under "Not yet in isim") |
| Types not yet in isim (iOS 18) | ❌ | 18.0 | not implemented, found by the 2026-10 sweep: `MapItemDetailSelectionAccessoryStyle`, `MKAddressFilter`, `MKLocalSearchRegionPriority`, `MKMapItemAnnotation`, `MKMapItemDetailViewController`, `MKMapItemDetailViewControllerDelegate`, `MKSelectionAccessory`, `MKSelectionAccessory.MapItemDetailPresentationStyle`, `MKSelectionAccessory.MapItemDetailPresentationStyle.CalloutStyle` (9 types; with their members under "Not yet in isim") |
| Geocoding (iOS 26): `MKGeocodingRequest`, `MKReverseGeocodingRequest` (`mapItems`, `getMapItems(completionHandler:)`, `cancel()`, `isCancelled`, `isLoading`, `preferredLocale`, `region`) | ✅ | 26.0 | adapted, offline: answered from Core Location's gazetteer (the places `CLGeocoder` and `MKLocalSearch` know); no match is `MKError.placemarkNotFound`, `ISIM_GEOCODER=offline` gives `serverFailure`. Tested (HelloMaps -geocode: test_geocoding_addresses_geojson) |
| Addresses (iOS 26): `MKAddress` (`fullAddress`, `shortAddress`), `MKAddressRepresentations` (`fullAddress(includingRegion:singleLine:)`, `cityName`, `cityWithContext`, `regionName`, `regionCode`), `MKMapItem` `init(location:address:)`, `location`, `address`, `addressRepresentations` | ✅ | 26.0 | adapted: built from the place's street, city, state, postal code and country (the city's context: its state in the United States, else its country). Tested (HelloMaps -geocode: test_geocoding_addresses_geojson) |
| `MKDistanceFormatter` (`string(fromDistance:)`, `distance(from:)`, `units`, `unitStyle`, `locale`) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: like Maps, metric (m below 1 km, km with one decimal below 10) or imperial (ft below 0.1 mi, or yd; mi with one decimal below 10); the locale's measurement system by default; abbreviated or full unit names. Tested (HelloMaps -geocode) |
| `MKGeoJSONDecoder`, `MKGeoJSONFeature` (`identifier`, `properties`, `geometry`), `MKGeoJSONObject` | ✅ | ≤17 | passthrough of the format (RFC 7946): Point → `MKPointAnnotation`, MultiPoint → `MKMultiPoint`, LineString → `MKPolyline`, MultiLineString → `MKMultiPolyline`, Polygon → `MKPolygon` (holes as interior polygons), MultiPolygon → `MKMultiPolygon`, GeometryCollection; malformed input throws `MKError.decodingFailed`. Tested (HelloMaps -geocode: shapes drawn on the map) |
| Launch options: `MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeKey` and the other keys, `MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeDriving` / `Walking` / `Transit` / `Cycling` / `Default` | ✅ | ≤17 | the constants; `openInMaps` logs and returns false (isim has no Maps app). Tested (HelloMaps -geocode) |
